### Problem: Longest arithmetic subsequence {#sec-lis-p3-arith}

::: {.p-statement}
Return the length of the longest arithmetic subsequence of `nums`. A sequence of length 2 or more is arithmetic when the difference between consecutive elements is constant. A single element is a trivial arithmetic subsequence of length 1.

$2 \le n \le 1000$. On $[3, 6, 9, 12]$ the answer is 4. On $[9, 4, 7, 2, 10]$ the answer is 3, the step $+3$ along $4, 7, 10$. On $[20, 1, 15, 3, 10, 5, 8]$ the answer is 4, the step $-5$ along $20, 15, 10, 5$.

Source: [LC 1027 · Longest Arithmetic Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-arithmetic-subsequence/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
An index can end many arithmetic subsequences, one per difference. The state cannot be the index alone: $[20, 1, 15, 3, 10, 5, 8]$ has a step of $-5$ and other steps ending at the same places. The previous element with the same difference is the predecessor, and a pair that has never been seen starts a sequence of length 2.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[i][d]$ = longest arithmetic subsequence ending at $i$ with difference $d$.
- **Transition.** For each $j < i$, let $d = a[i] - a[j]$. Then $dp[i][d] = dp[j][d] + 1$, and a missing $dp[j][d]$ counts as 1 (the single element $a[j]$).
- **Answer.** The maximum value written, which is at least 2 when $n \ge 2$. **Order.** Increasing $i$, and every earlier $j$.
:::

The difference of a fixed value is the one-dimensional value DP already on the practice ladder: one map from value to length, because the step never changes. Here the step is chosen by the pair, so the map hangs off the index.

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i, d)` is the longest arithmetic subsequence ending at `i` with difference `d`. It extends an earlier index that realises the same difference. A first pair has length 2. The answer tries every pair as the last step, which fixes `d`.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("arith", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "4"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arith-rec
def arith_rec(a):
    def f(i, d):
        best = 2
        for j in range(i):
            if a[i] - a[j] == d:
                best = max(best, 2 if j == 0 else 1 + f(j, d))
        return best

    ans = 1
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(i):
            ans = max(ans, f(i, a[i] - a[j]))
    return ans
```

##### C++

```cpp
int arithRec(int i, long long d, const vector<int>& a) {
    int best = 2;
    for (int j = 0; j < i; ++j)
        if ((long long)a[i] - a[j] == d)
            best = max(best, j == 0 ? 2 : 1 + arithRec(j, d, a));
    return best;
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
The pair `(i, d)` repeats as soon as two different later elements ask for the same last step. Store the pair. Differences can be negative, so the key is the integer `d`, not an array index.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("arith", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "4"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arith-memo
def arith_memo(a):
    memo = {}

    def f(i, d):
        if (i, d) not in memo:
            best = 2
            for j in range(i):
                if a[i] - a[j] == d:
                    best = max(best, 2 if j == 0 else 1 + f(j, d))
            memo[i, d] = best
        return memo[i, d]

    ans = 1
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(i):
            ans = max(ans, f(i, a[i] - a[j]))
    return ans
```

##### C++

```cpp
int arithMemo(int i, long long d, const vector<int>& a, map<pair<int, long long>, int>& memo) {
    auto key = make_pair(i, d);
    if (memo.count(key)) return memo[key];
    int best = 2;
    for (int j = 0; j < i; ++j)
        if ((long long)a[i] - a[j] == d)
            best = max(best, j == 0 ? 2 : 1 + arithMemo(j, d, a, memo));
    return memo[key] = best;
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
`dp[i]` is a map from difference to length. For every earlier `j`, the difference `a[i] - a[j]` extends `dp[j]` of that same difference, or starts at 2. The answer is the largest length written.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("arith", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "4"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arith-tab
def arith_tab(a):
    dp = [{} for _ in a]
    ans = 1
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        for j in range(i):
            d = x - a[j]
            dp[i][d] = max(dp[i].get(d, 0), dp[j].get(d, 1) + 1)
            ans = max(ans, dp[i][d])
    return ans
```

##### C++

```cpp
int arithTab(const vector<int>& a) {
    int n = a.size(), ans = 1;
    vector<map<long long, int>> dp(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        for (int j = 0; j < i; ++j) {
            long long d = (long long)a[i] - a[j];
            int got = dp[j].count(d) ? dp[j][d] + 1 : 2;
            dp[i][d] = max(dp[i][d], got);
            ans = max(ans, dp[i][d]);
        }
    return ans;
}
```
:::

#### One difference

::: {.form-next}
When the difference is given, the state collapses to a map from the value to the best length: `best[x] = best[x - d] + 1`. This button is that program, run on every difference that actually occurs between a pair, which is how the three samples stay small. The table above is the same idea with the difference stored beside the index instead of being fixed outside the loop.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("arith", "fix")
    assert str(final) == "4"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arith-fix
def arith_fixed(a, d):
    best = {}
    ans = 1
    for x in a:
        best[x] = best.get(x - d, 0) + 1
        ans = max(ans, best[x])
    return ans

def arith_by_diff(a):
    diffs = {a[i] - a[j] for i in range(len(a)) for j in range(i)}
    return max([1] + [arith_fixed(a, d) for d in diffs])

assert arith_rec([3, 6, 9, 12]) == 4
assert arith_memo([3, 6, 9, 12]) == arith_tab([3, 6, 9, 12]) == 4
assert arith_tab([9, 4, 7, 2, 10]) == 3
assert arith_tab([20, 1, 15, 3, 10, 5, 8]) == 4
assert arith_fixed([3, 6, 9, 12], 3) == 4
assert arith_by_diff([9, 4, 7, 2, 10]) == 3
assert arith_by_diff([20, 1, 15, 3, 10, 5, 8]) == 4
assert arith_tab([1, 2]) == 2 and arith_tab([5]) == 1
```

##### C++

```cpp
int arithFixed(const vector<int>& a, long long d) {
    map<long long, int> best;
    int ans = 1;
    for (int x : a) {
        best[x] = best[x - d] + 1;
        ans = max(ans, best[x]);
    }
    return ans;
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** and **memoisation** are $O(n^2)$ states times a scan, so write the **table**, which is $O(n^2)$ time and $O(n^2)$ maps in the worst case. **One difference** is $O(n)$ after the difference is known, and trying every occurring difference is another $O(n^2)$. $n \le 1000$. Differences reach $2 \times 10^9$ in absolute value and can be negative: store them in a map, or shift them if you insist on an array.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Two elements: the answer is 2, whatever the difference.
- One element: the answer is 1. The loops never write a pair.
- A negative step is ordinary. $20, 15, 10, 5$ is difference $-5$, not a reversed copy of a positive problem you forgot to run.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- One length per index. Several differences end at the same index. Keeping only the longest of them drops a shorter chain that a later element wanted to extend.
- A fresh pair read as length 0. The predecessor alone already has length 1, so the pair has length 2. `dp[j].get(d, 1) + 1` is that 2.
- A 32-bit difference. $a[i] - a[j]$ overflows a 32-bit signed integer at the extremes. Subtract in 64 bits.
:::

**Variants.** A difference given in the input is `arith_fixed`: [LC 1218 · Longest Arithmetic Subsequence of Given Difference](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-arithmetic-subsequence-of-given-difference/){difficulty="Medium"}. A Fibonacci subsequence forces the next value, so the predecessor of a pair is a hash lookup: [LC 873 · Length of Longest Fibonacci Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/length-of-longest-fibonacci-subsequence/){difficulty="Medium"}. Counting the arithmetic subsequences of length at least 3 adds the counts instead of taking a maximum: [LC 446 · Arithmetic Slices II - Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/arithmetic-slices-ii-subsequence/){difficulty="Hard"}. Three terms of a geometric progression are the same pair with a product: [CF 567C · Geometric Progression](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/567/C){rating="1700"}.
